title: Midcontinent Rift
summary: About 1.1 billion years ago the North American continent began to split apart along the Midcontinent Rift, which at its peak stretched over 3,000 km. Huge volumes of lava poured out, but the break failed; the basalts are now exposed mainly around Lake Superior and buried elsewhere.

uncertainty.note: Sources give only an approximate start of about 1.1 billion years ago; no end date or duration was read.

where.modern_name: Lake Superior region, North America (proxy pin at Lake Superior; rift ran from Kansas through Lake Superior to Lower Michigan)
where.historical_name: Laurentia interior, pre-Pangaean North America (no named polity)

paleo.not_applicable: Outline record; paleo reconstruction not done. Pin is a modern proxy.

importance.justification: The largest known failed continental rift, source of the Lake Superior flood basalts and Keweenaw copper.

sources.title: The Midcontinent Rift
sources.publisher: U.S. National Park Service, Keweenaw National Historical Park

sources.title: Better late than never - making a billion-year-old geologic feature great again

reviewer_note: Date is only 'about 1.1 billion years ago'; pin is a proxy at Lake Superior (coordinates from a non-authoritative site) for a feature over 3,000 km long; precision label is approximate.
